text:
perf-bot: Nightly perf CI alert: p95 latency increased ~28% on small-batch suite (model: mix-small-quant). Report: https://ci.internal/reports/4471123581
riley: saw the alert. thanks perf-bot. @camille can you pick this up? I'm mid-bisect on a separate flaky test.
camille: on it, grabbing logs now.
riley: quick baseline numbers from the dashboard: p95 baseline ~310ms -> current ~400ms.
sacha: any config/deploy diffs in the 02:00-03:00 UTC window? I can check deploy history.
camille: checking commit window — last deploy 02:15 UTC changed kernel-selection heuristics (rev: a1b2c3).
sacha: ok i'll run a local replica on that rev with the small-batch profile.
camille: kicking a repro: `./tools/run_bench --profile small-batch --rev a1b2c3`
camille: logs show: "kv_cache hit rate stable, scheduler wait +~30ms"
ben: could be the scheduler yield tweak. pinging eng-runtime-scheduler infra.
eng-scheduler-bot: Created incident SCHED-447 - possible scheduler-yield regression. PagerDuty notified.
riley: good catch. @sacha please attach the flamegraph when available.
sacha: will post link shortly.
camille: quick local repro shows ~+22% p95, diff pasted: https://paste.internal/4471123581
sacha: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/fg/4471123581
ben: reading flamegraph — heavy time in spin_wait() now, wasn't present pre-a1b2c3.
riley: plan proposal: revert the kernel-selection heuristic in canary, rerun nightly/dry-run. If that drops p95 we promote.
camille: opening revert PR + will request a dry-run: https://git/repo/pulls/1223
release-bot: Dry-run scheduled for canary at 03:40 UTC (PR 1223).
riley: nice. if dry-run shows regression gone we'll roll back. if not, escalate to kernel/infra.
sacha: analysis + dry-run results ETA ~45m.
camille: adding a note to the runbook: "small-batch: check scheduler spin/wait traces and kernel-selection revs".
riley: thanks all — i'll update the nightly alert runbook and ping support if we roll back.
ben: :thumbsup:
camille: ping me if anything blocks the revert or I/O access for the canary dry-run."
